name: MuQ / MuQ-MuLan
type: Feature extractor (MuQ) plus a zero-shot music-text joint embedding classifier (MuQ-MuLan, CLAP-style contrastive dual encoder) -- usable for zero-shot music/tag classification via audio-text cosine similarity, not a fingerprint identifier
maintainer: Tencent AI Lab (github.com/tencent-ailab/MuQ), weights published under the community 'OpenMuQ' organization on Hugging Face; paper released January 2025
method: Embedding-based. MuQ: self-supervised pretraining using Mel-RVQ (Mel-domain Residual Vector Quantization) tokenization with iterative masked-prediction training (scaled from 0.9K to 160K hours of open data). MuQ-MuLan: a CLIP/CLAP-style contrastive dual encoder pairing the MuQ audio tower with a bilingual (English/Chinese) text tower, trained on music-text pairs, enabling zero-shot classification by computing cosine similarity between an audio embedding and candidate text-prompt embeddings (e.g. a 'music' vs 'speech' prompt pair).
required_input: Raw audio waveform at 24 kHz (librosa `sr=24000` in official usage examples); MuQ-MuLan additionally takes free-text prompts (English or Chinese) for the text tower
minimum_clip_length: Not explicitly documented by the authors; practically used with clip lengths of a few seconds to ~10s for tagging, similar to other MIR embedding models. [uncertain] exact minimum
classification_or_hitrate: MuQ-MuLan achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot music tagging on MagnaTagATune top-50 tags: ROC-AUC 79.3 / PR-AUC 29.3, beating MuLan (ROC-AUC 78.2, despite MuLan using ~3x more pretraining data) and LAION-CLAP/Microsoft CLAP baselines. The standalone MuQ encoder reaches SOTA or near-SOTA on several MARBLE-suite MIR probing tasks with as little as 0.9K hours of open pretraining data, improving further at 160K hours. No published binary music-vs-non-music/speech accuracy number was found. [uncertain]
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: No published evaluation for nightcore, sped-up/slowed edits, pitch-shifted reuploads, live versions, or cover-song robustness. [uncertain]
catalog_language_bias: MuQ-MuLan's text tower is explicitly bilingual (English + Chinese), a notable differentiator versus English-only CLAP/MERT-family models, suggesting comparatively stronger alignment for C-pop / Chinese-market text-audio matching given Tencent's data provenance; no formal per-region breakdown (K-pop/J-pop/anime/VTuber/indie) has been published. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: MagnaTagATune (zero-shot tagging headline result) plus the MARBLE benchmark suite (GTZAN, GiantSteps, MTG-Jamendo, etc.) for the underlying MuQ encoder
confidence_calibration: Output is a continuous cosine-similarity score between an audio embedding and a text-prompt embedding, not a calibrated probability -- as with CLAP-family models, a usable decision threshold must be empirically tuned per deployment; the authors do not publish calibration/threshold guidance. [uncertain]
api_availability: Free, self-hosted only -- weights downloadable via Hugging Face (OpenMuQ org) and GitHub (tencent-ailab/MuQ), no API keys or hosted inference service; code is MIT-licensed, but model weights are separately licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial use only, per the repo's LICENSE_weights file).
chrome_extension_usability: No confirmed ONNX / Transformers.js / browser-ready deployment found for MuQ or MuQ-MuLan as of research date -- inference requires PyTorch. Not usable directly inside a Chrome extension without a backend. [uncertain] on whether a community ONNX port exists.
audio_access_requirement: Requires raw audio bytes at 24 kHz. Same chrome.tabCapture/offscreen-document, user-gesture, tab-mute, and DRM/age-restriction constraints as any other audio-based method in this comparison set.
client_vs_server: Given no browser runtime, audio must be sent from the user's machine to a backend server running PyTorch for inference -- not client-only.
bundle_weight_cold_start: MuQ (~300M params) plus MuQ-MuLan's added text/audio contrastive towers (~700M params combined) -- a multi-hundred-MB to multi-GB checkpoint, far too large for an extension bundle; would be server-hosted, with cold start from one-time model load plus per-request inference latency.
breakage_risk: Young project (paper published January 2025) with an actively maintained GitHub repo from a corporate lab (Tencent AI Lab) as of research date; smaller and less battle-tested community footprint than MERT, and no PyPI package was found, so tooling maturity risk is somewhat higher than more established alternatives. [uncertain]
realtime_capability: No published inference-latency benchmark; the combined MuQ + MuQ-MuLan model (~1B parameters total) implies GPU-class compute is needed for near-real-time use, but exact browser-relevant timing figures were not found. [uncertain]
identification_fields: None directly -- zero-shot classification via MuQ-MuLan yields a similarity/tag score against arbitrary text prompts (e.g. genre, mood, or a 'music' vs 'speech' prompt), not title, artist, album, or ISRC; it is not a catalog-backed identification system.
karaoke_specific_outputs: No native BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental activity, or word-level timing output shipped out of the box; the underlying MuQ encoder can in principle be probed/fine-tuned for MIR tasks like key estimation (as covered by the MARBLE suite) but nothing karaoke-specific is provided directly. [uncertain]
tos_restrictions: CC-BY-NC-4.0 on the model weights explicitly prohibits commercial use, identical in effect to MERT's licensing constraint -- a material blocker for a publicly distributed Chrome extension without a separate commercial license from Tencent AI Lab.
risk_tolerance_note: Same category as MERT: an explicit, unambiguous legal license restriction (non-commercial), not a widely-tolerated unofficial-surface gray area like ytInitialData scraping or SongRec -- deployment in a shipped product would need direct legal clearance.
cascade_position: Enrichment/fallback role -- zero-shot text-prompted classification (e.g. against 'music' vs 'speech'/'noise' prompts) could serve as a secondary check when cheaper heuristics are inconclusive, but its compute cost and server dependency make it unsuitable as the primary always-on gate.
failure_mode: Zero-shot similarity scoring against arbitrary text prompts is a known CLAP-family weak point -- it can produce a confidently high similarity score for out-of-distribution or ambiguous audio, risking a visible, confidently-wrong music/non-music classification if not backed by a carefully tuned threshold or secondary check.
cost_model_at_scale: No vendor per-query fee (self-hosted); compute cost scales with the larger combined model size (~1B params) relative to MERT, so per-inference server cost is proportionally higher at equivalent usage volume.
geo_region_availability: No geo-gating -- globally downloadable from Hugging Face/GitHub; the bilingual English/Chinese design makes it specifically attractive for C-pop-heavy catalogs relative to English-only alternatives like CLAP.
